verses.english: Numbered Discourses 5.31
4. With Sumanā
With Sumanā
At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

verses.pali: Atha kho sumanā rājakumārī pañcahi rathasatehi pañcahi rājakumārisatehi parivutā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho sumanā rājakumārī bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Princess Sumanā, escorted by five hundred chariots and five hundred royal maidens, went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

verses.pali: “Idhassu, bhante, bhagavato dve sāvakā samasaddhā samasīlā samapaññā—
verses.english: “Sir, suppose there were two disciples equal in faith, ethics, and wisdom.
One is a giver, one is not.

verses.pali: Te kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjeyyuṁ.
verses.english: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

verses.pali: Devabhūtānaṁ pana nesaṁ, bhante, siyā viseso, siyā nānākaraṇan”ti?
verses.english: When they have become gods, would there be any distinction or difference between them?”
“There would be, Sumanā,” said the Buddha.

verses.pali: “yo so, sumane, dāyako so amuṁ adāyakaṁ devabhūto samāno pañcahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhāti—
verses.english: “As a god, the one who was a giver surpasses the other in five respects:

verses.pali: dibbena āyunā, dibbena vaṇṇena, dibbena sukhena, dibbena yasena, dibbena ādhipateyyena.
verses.english: heavenly lifespan, beauty, happiness, glory, and sovereignty.

verses.pali: Yo so, sumane, dāyako so amuṁ adāyakaṁ devabhūto samāno imehi pañcahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhāti”.
verses.english: As a god, the one who was a giver surpasses the other in these five respects.”

verses.pali: “Sace pana te, bhante, tato cutā itthattaṁ āgacchanti, manussabhūtānaṁ pana nesaṁ, bhante, siyā viseso, siyā nānākaraṇan”ti?
verses.english: “But sir, if they pass away from there and come back to this place as human beings, would there still be any distinction or difference between them?”
“There would be, Sumanā,” said the Buddha.

verses.pali: “yo so, sumane, dāyako so amuṁ adāyakaṁ manussabhūto samāno pañcahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhāti—
verses.english: “As a human being, the one who was a giver would surpass the other in five respects:

verses.pali: mānusakena āyunā, mānusakena vaṇṇena, mānusakena sukhena, mānusakena yasena, mānusakena ādhipateyyena.
verses.english: human lifespan, beauty, happiness, glory, and sovereignty.

verses.pali: Yo so, sumane, dāyako so amuṁ adāyakaṁ manussabhūto samāno imehi pañcahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhāti”.
verses.english: As a human being, the one who was a giver surpasses the other in these five respects.”

verses.pali: “Sace pana te, bhante, ubho agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, pabbajitānaṁ pana nesaṁ, bhante, siyā viseso, siyā nānākaraṇan”ti?
verses.english: “But sir, if they both go forth from the lay life to homelessness, would there still be any distinction or difference between them?”
“There would be, Sumanā,” said the Buddha.

verses.pali: “yo so, sumane, dāyako so amuṁ adāyakaṁ pabbajito samāno pañcahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhāti—
verses.english: “As a renunciate, the one who was a giver surpasses the other in five respects.

verses.pali: yācitova bahulaṁ cīvaraṁ paribhuñjati appaṁ ayācito, yācitova bahulaṁ piṇḍapātaṁ paribhuñjati appaṁ ayācito, yācitova bahulaṁ senāsanaṁ paribhuñjati appaṁ ayācito, yācitova bahulaṁ gilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṁ paribhuñjati appaṁ ayācito.
verses.english: They usually use only what they’ve been invited to accept—robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick—rarely using them without invitation.

verses.pali: Yehi kho pana sabrahmacārīhi saddhiṁ viharati tyassa manāpeneva bahulaṁ kāyakammena samudācaranti appaṁ amanāpena, manāpeneva bahulaṁ vacīkammena samudācaranti appaṁ amanāpena, manāpeneva bahulaṁ manokammena samudācaranti appaṁ amanāpena, manāpaṁyeva bahulaṁ upahāraṁ upaharanti appaṁ amanāpaṁ.
verses.english: When living with other spiritual practitioners, they usually find themselves treated agreeably by them by way of body, speech, and mind, and rarely disagreeably. And they are usually presented with agreeable things by them, rarely with disagreeable ones.

verses.pali: Yo so, sumane, dāyako so amuṁ adāyakaṁ pabbajito samāno imehi pañcahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhātī”ti.
verses.english: As a renunciate, the one who was a giver surpasses the other in these five respects.”

verses.pali: “Sace pana te, bhante, ubho arahattaṁ pāpuṇanti, arahattappattānaṁ pana nesaṁ, bhante, siyā viseso, siyā nānākaraṇan”ti?
verses.english: “But sir, if they both attain perfection, as perfected ones would there still be any distinction or difference between them?”

verses.pali: “Ettha kho panesāhaṁ, sumane, na kiñci nānākaraṇaṁ vadāmi, yadidaṁ vimuttiyā vimuttin”ti.
verses.english: “In that case, I say there is no difference between the freedom of one and the freedom of the other.”
“It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing!

verses.pali: Yāvañcidaṁ, bhante, alameva dānāni dātuṁ alaṁ puññāni kātuṁ;
verses.english: This is quite enough to justify giving gifts and making merit.

verses.pali: yatra hi nāma devabhūtassāpi upakārāni puññāni, manussabhūtassāpi upakārāni puññāni, pabbajitassāpi upakārāni puññānī”ti.
verses.english: For merit is helpful for those who have become gods, human beings, and renunciates.”
“That’s so true, Sumanā.

verses.pali: Alañhi, sumane, dānāni dātuṁ alaṁ puññāni kātuṁ.
verses.english: It’s quite enough to justify giving gifts and making merit.

verses.pali: Devabhūtassāpi upakārāni puññāni, manussabhūtassāpi upakārāni puññāni, pabbajitassāpi upakārāni puññānī”ti.
verses.english: For merit is helpful for those who have become gods, human beings, and renunciates.”
That is what the Buddha said.

verses.pali: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato athāparaṁ etadavoca satthā:
verses.english: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“The moon so immaculate,
journeying across the dimension of space;
outshines with its radiance
all the world’s stars.
So too, a faithful individual,
perfect in ethics,
outshines with their generosity
all the world’s stingy people.
The thundering rain cloud,
its hundred peaks wreathed in lightning,
pours down over the rich earth,
soaking the uplands and valleys.
Even so, an astute person accomplished in vision,
a disciple of the fully awakened Buddha,
surpasses a stingy person
in five respects:
long life and fame,
beauty and happiness.
Lavished with riches,
they depart to rejoice in heaven.”
